description: How should domain concepts handle concurrent access and modifications?
question: What is your default approach for handling concurrency in the domain?

options.name: Optimistic Locking
options.description: Assume conflicts are rare. Check version/timestamp at save time. Fail if modified by another.
options.when_to_use: Read-heavy workloads, conflicts rare, user can retry, web applications
options.example: Order has version. Save fails with ConcurrencyException if version changed since load

options.name: Pessimistic Locking
options.description: Lock resources when accessed. Other requests wait or fail. Guarantees exclusive access.
options.when_to_use: High-conflict scenarios, critical resources, short transactions, database support
options.example: Order.LockForProcessing() acquires exclusive lock. Other processes wait until released

options.name: Aggregate Boundaries
options.description: Consistency enforced within aggregate boundary. Different aggregates are eventually consistent.
options.when_to_use: DDD approach, scalability priority, distributed systems, clear ownership boundaries
options.example: Order aggregate is consistent. Inventory aggregate updated eventually via events

options.name: Immutable Objects
options.description: Objects don't change after creation. New versions created instead. No concurrent modification possible.
options.when_to_use: Functional approach, audit trail, temporal queries, thread safety, event sourcing
options.example: Order is immutable. Order.WithNewLineItem() returns new Order instance

options.name: Command Serialization
options.description: Serialize commands for same aggregate. Process one at a time. Queue ensures order.
options.when_to_use: Event sourcing, actor model, strict ordering required, high contention
options.example: Commands for Order-123 processed sequentially by OrderActor. No concurrent modification
